title: Where I am right now
content:
My monthly expenses are around 45k, non-negotiable — basically EMI plus money I send to family. Then comes rent and living expenses in Bangalore, which comes to about 40k. Whatever's left goes into personal savings (10-20k a month), something I only started a few months ago.

On the work side: I'm currently working as a Business Analyst at Plivo, on automations and AI/low-code, trying to automate the US support tickets we get from customers. It's been three months with little progress — mainly because I've only been working on the prompt and haven't actually researched what I could be missing.

Back to money: my runway is only 3 months (and that's assuming I eat nothing and live on the streets) if my job disappears tomorrow. I don't like this number and want to make it go away, which basically needs a lottery. But realistically, if I plan for it, I need at least 6 months of runway including food and rent, which comes to 6 lakhs. At my current savings rate, it'll take me 60 months to get there in the worst case (5 years), or 2-2.5 years (~30 months) if I save aggressively. This means no car and no flat of my own in Bangalore for the next 5 years if I stick to my current skills, job, and salary — and I'll be 31 by then. All things I'd hoped for, and half-seriously thought I'd have achieved much earlier, maybe back in childhood.

The house loan — 50 lakhs over 17 years, floating interest rate — is really my main headache, hence the lottery wish. But it means my parents have a roof over their heads, a good one, and if things get really bad, we have stuff to sell. Let's hope I don't have to sell my body.

So, first goal: get the support automation working. I've finally set a deadline for myself, end of this month, and honestly for my manager and a colleague too. Beyond that, I need to upskill, and I can't spend recklessly anymore like I used to. All leisure and luxury have to go out the window, which is easy for me since I don't go out much anyway. But considering I need to upskill and keep my brain trained without slipping further into feeling depressed, I have to actually use the Cult membership I already have — swim, and get out and run. So yeah, that's where I am right now.

Tomorrow: where I want to be. A very delusional blog, that one's going to be.

title: Lemon v2: the living room
content: Rebuilt lemon from scratch. v1 proved an LLM could puppet a pixel-art character; v2 is the actual game. New 480x270 renderer, a 141-action engine so the character can genuinely move — sit, pace, curl up, come apart — and a brain grounded in motivational interviewing, red-teamed so you can't just command someone out of a depressive episode. The model speaks through a single @@hope|mood|act@@ tag the engine reads to drive the animation. You talk a person out of their room; it only opens up if you actually listen. Free-tier Groq to Gemini proxy behind it. Live.

title: Shipping with Fable 5
content: Late-night session with Claude Fable 5: built and deployed two projects in 47 minutes. A WebGL train-robbery animation (now gamified with bounties and a day/night cycle) and mypager — a password-locked whiteboard that syncs encrypted notes through a private GitHub repo. Five commits, two repos, both live on GitHub Pages. Receipts in the picture.
